text:
incident-bot: P1 page for customer tenant 'acme-corp' in VPC-dedicated pool — observed sudden KV/prefix cache hit-rate collapse, affecting tail latency and token cost. Paging on-call SRE.

jess: saw the page, I'm on. seeing prefix_hit_rate drop from ~88% to ~4% on tenant acme-corp across pool-42. all requests are still processed but 95th latency jumped and cost spiked.

matt: on my way, pulling last 15m metrics. can you paste the query?

jess: metrics query: `sum(rate(prefix_hits[5m])) / sum(rate(prefix_lookups[5m])) * 100` — running now.

kai: i've got logs showing a surge of new prefixes from a nightly batch job around 03:12 UTC. looks like many long keys, e.g. `user-exports/2026-03-15/*` filled the prefix space.

jess: that would pollute prefix cache. anything that indicates eviction churn?

kai: yes, eviction rate spiked 30x. snippet: ```evictions: 18324 -> 548000; mem_used: 92% -> 99%```

matt: evidence that tenant's batch job is creating high-cardinality prefixes. cache TTLs are short so prefix cache thrash.

jess: immediate mitigation options: 1) disable prefix caching for acme-corp 2) bump their cache quota 3) route traffic to larger dedicated fallback pool 4) ask customer to back off job.

olivia: I'll draft a heads-up to the customer in parallel. want to get a mitigation first before telling them to pause.

matt: prioritizing quick mitigations. i'll try #1 from control plane: `redwoodctl cache-set --tenant acme-corp --prefix-caching off`

kai: if we disable prefix caching, throughput drops but latency should normalize and cost will go up slightly. agree.

jess: do it, and also enable fallback routing to pool-99: `redwoodctl route set --tenant acme-corp --fallback-pool pool-99`

matt: ran disable command, got `200 OK` from control plane. applying fallback route now.

support-bot: Deploy ID dpl-3461 started: applying routing changes to pool-99 (ETA ~35s).

matt: routing change completed. monitoring.

kai: initial metrics: prefix_hit_rate now reported as N/A (disabled) but token latency 95th reduced from 1.8s to 650ms. cost rate elevated ~+22% but stable. evictions dropped immediately.

jess: good. put an alert suppression on the page so it doesn't keep paging the team while we stabilize.

matt: suppression in place for 30m. creating followup action: roll a tenant-specific cache-config that blocks extremely high-cardinality prefix patterns and raises quota thresholds for canary.

olivia: customer message draft: "Hi Acme team — we detected a spike of high-cardinality prefixes from a recent export job that caused cache thrash in your VPC pool. We've temporarily disabled prefix caching and routed traffic to a larger pool to stabilize latency. We recommend pausing the export while we work with you on a long-term fix. We'll follow up with specific remediation steps and timeline." Want to add anything?

jess: add that we can provide a safe config change to their job to shard keys or add a single static prefix for exports. also offer a postmortem and quota bump discussion.

olivia: sent message to primary contact and added a short incident note with mitigation steps.

kai: next steps on infra: implement tenant-level prefix blacklist and an adaptive TTL increase for heavy prefixes. I'll open an eng issue and tag runtime + infra.

matt: assigning to eng-runtime, cc eng-infra. will schedule canary release for the blacklist into dedicated pools only first.

jess: handoff to matt is complete for runbook items. i'll remain the incident lead until we have the postmortem outline.

matt: i'll monitor for next 2 hours then hand back. thanks all. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident P1 (1802500000) status: mitigated -> stable. page closed at 1802500545. next: postmortem in #postmortems within 48h.
